extracted.intended_audience: researchers, funders, and policymakers interested in science funding, grant evaluation, and science-of-science studies
extracted.subtask_description: Empirical analysis of how promotional language in grant proposals relates to funding probability, inferred innovativeness, and downstream scientific impact, using large-scale full-text semantic analysis and an experiment. Useful for understanding evaluative signals in grant-writing and review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Percentage of promotional language in a grant proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: The percentage of promotional language in a grant proposal is associated with up to a doubling of the grant's probability of being funded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measured as the share of text classified as promotional language; shown in large-scale observational analysis across NIH, NSF, and Novo Nordisk Foundation grants to strongly associate with funding success. Use as an evaluative signal when modeling funding probability, while noting observational associations may be confounded without experimental controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotional language as a signal of originality and significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Promotional language purportedly may convey an innovative idea's originality and significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret promotional language not merely as rhetorical flourish but as a communicative signal about an idea's merit. Consider both how often and how strongly claims about novelty/significance are expressed when assessing perceived innovativeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotional language reflects intrinsic innovativeness
rubrics_metrics.description: A grant's promotional language reflects its intrinsic level of innovativeness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promotional language correlates with measures of intrinsic innovativeness in the authors' analyses; thus promotional phrasing may act as an imperfect proxy for substantive novelty. Use cautiously alongside content-based measures of novelty to avoid conflating rhetoric with substantive contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotional language predicts downstream citation and productivity impact
rubrics_metrics.description: The percentage of promotional language predicts the expected citation and productivity impact of publications that are supported by funded grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promotional language is associated not only with funding outcomes but with subsequent scientific impact of supported work. When evaluating proposals, consider promotional language as one predictive feature among others for downstream impact modeling; validate against longitudinal citation/productivity data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotional language can causally communicate merit via cognitive activation
rubrics_metrics.description: A computer-assisted experiment that manipulates the promotional language demonstrates how promotional language can communicate the merit of ideas through cognitive activation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experimental evidence indicates promotional wording can change readers' cognitive responses and thus causally influence perceptions of merit. This supports treating promotional language as an active communicative tool rather than only a correlational marker; however, consider ethical and fairness implications of leveraging rhetoric in evaluations.
